description:
Payments / Infrastructure Engineer, Series A fintech
 Location: San Francisco, CA (in person)
 Partnership: EQL Tech has been exclusively retained by a fast-growing fintech to hire the engineer who owns its money-movement and platform stack: card issuing, ledger integrity and reconciliation, CI/CD, monitoring, and scaling from hundreds of cardholders to hundreds of thousands.
 About the company and the mission
 The company is building the financial rails that let families use state education funds (Education Savings Accounts, or ESAs). The $900B US public education budget is being opened up so parents can direct their share, on average $7.5k per child per year. Families get instant access to their funds through a card, and states get automated fraud detection. The product is live in Arizona, growing fast, and expanding to Florida and federal programs. The company has raised $16M from top-tier VCs and angels.
 The team
 A small, in-person team in San Francisco, most of them ex-founders. The founders are engineers who ran their own alternative school together: one was a quant at Goldman Sachs, the other built the computer vision system for the world's largest smart warehousing company at 19. You will work alongside a founding engineer from AI research at MILA, a Head of Risk who led risk at Mercury, Stripe and Circle, a Payments Engineer from Microsoft billing and Goldman Sachs payments security, and the former Deputy Director of Arizona's ESA department.
 The role
 This is one role, not two. Anyone strong at distributed systems and high-throughput data work is good at both the money-movement side and the platform side. You will own the reliability, scalability and correctness of the stack that moves every dollar.
 Money movement: ledgered internal state, transaction lifecycle, idempotency, retries and deterministic replay, so every flow can be reasoned about.
 Reconciliation: continuous reconciliation across the internal ledger, card network events, banking events and partner reports, plus the tooling to chase a mismatch to its root fast.
 Guardrails: stop bad states before they happen: double spend, duplicate webhook processing, inconsistent balances, orphaned settlements.
 Card issuing and banking integrations: own the integrations with card issuing, banking and disbursement partners, and the reporting the bank and regulators depend on.
 Platform: CI/CD, monitoring, security, and the infrastructure to take the system from hundreds of cardholders to hundreds of thousands through spiky demand without dropping or duplicating an event.
 Requirements 
 Your profile
 2+ years building distributed systems that handle high data throughput, with some security exposure. You do not need to have worked in fintech: trading firms, cloud infrastructure teams, cybersecurity companies and large consumer platforms all build these skills.
 You have owned something end to end. You designed it, shipped it, ran it and lived with the architecture calls. A system you personally led matters more than the size of the company it was at.
 Obsessive about correctness. Retries don't erase history, idempotency is deliberate, and validation belongs where truth lives.
 You assume the real world is unreliable. Banks go down, queues back up, vendors change APIs. Reliable to you means the same behaviour at 10 payments or 10,000,000.
 AI native, not AI dependent. You use tools like Claude Code to move faster, and you still do your own thinking.
 The mission matters to you. No education background needed, but giving families real choice over their kids' education has to mean something to you.
 Able to work in person with the team in San Francisco . Visa sponsorship available.
 Experience with card issuing, banking rails, ledgers or reconciliation is a strong plus, not a requirement.
 Benefits 
 Compensation and benefits
 Salary: $125,000 to $200,000+, depending on experience.
 Meaningful founding equity. 
 Health: medical, dental and vision (up to 100% of premium for you and your dependents), life insurance, a health FSA and a 401(k).
 Visa sponsorship available.
 Impact: shape how the $900B US public education budget reaches families.
 How they hire
 An intro call with a founder, a technical deep dive with the CTO, a take-home built from a real problem that you present on a whiteboard, then a short paid work trial in the office. Open books throughout: ask them anything.
